rows.backtranslation: Use a number: lower bound ≤ number ≤ upper bound.
rows.caller_scope: NumericSlider error after toIntOrNull or an out-of-range Int. %1$s is minimum and %2$s maximum, both Int arguments rendered as strings. Both boundaries are inclusive. This generic error retains the generic English number wording; the separate whole-number dialog prompt remains a held gap. It does not assert that fractions are accepted or replace integer parsing.
rows.confidence: Moderate source/compositional functional instruction; mathematical notation in prose. No native/layout certificate.
rows.independent_semantic_review: Own use-number instruction plus inclusive mathematical interval keeps exact minimum/maximum slots. Actual parser is integer, but this generic error neither promises fractions nor loses an explicit integer requirement from this English source; separate whole-number prompt remains untranslated.

rows.backtranslation: Size: use a number greater than 0.
rows.caller_scope: NormalizeImagesDialog value() must parse finite >0 input. Pixel mode requires numerical whole values; percentage mode permits positive decimals; percentage is relative to the current largest placed dimension of the selected axis. The result rounds into 1..Int.MAX_VALUE. This deliberately generic positive-size prompt retains source specificity rather than incorrectly requiring typed ≥1 or disallowing decimal percentages. No upper size, source cap, RAM fit or successful normalization is promised.
rows.confidence: Moderate source/compositional functional instruction; mathematical notation in prose. No native/layout certificate.
rows.independent_semantic_review: Spatial size + use-number >0 retains generic source condition. Percentage mode allows positive fractions and resolves against largest selected-axis placement; no typed >=1 constraint, integer-only restriction or budget success introduced.

rows.caller_scope: TextStyleDialog text size is parsed by uiNumber, converted to Float and accepted within inclusive 1f..1024f. Decimal keyboard is enabled. Fractions such as 1.5 px are allowed. This is font size, not integer bitmap width/height, memory budget or percentage. Mathematical bounds preserve both endpoints without adding whole/integer.
rows.confidence: Moderate source/compositional functional instruction; mathematical notation in prose. No native/layout certificate.
rows.independent_semantic_review: Inclusive range and px explicitly remain in the error for Float text size. Fractions allowed. Not bitmap dimensions or a memory estimate.

rows.backtranslation: Width and height: use numbers greater than 0. The image you want: width at least 1 pixel and height at least 1 pixel.
rows.caller_scope: DimensionControls first requires finite raw numbers >0, with whole numerical pixel values but decimal percentages allowed; it converts percentages against original per-axis bases, rounds and accepts only 1..Int.MAX_VALUE on each axis. The first clause addresses entered width/height values >0. The second explicitly describes the desired image in px and requires ≥1 separately on width and height, preserving the resolved-output distinction without telling the user to enter ≥1 percent. This is an authored functional paraphrase: it does not introduce an unattested verb for resolve/convert. It neither promises that every positive input works nor claims raw values are already px. Aspect locking may update the opposite field before both are validated; separate consumer memory/source limits remain outside this prompt.
rows.confidence: Moderate source/compositional functional instruction; mathematical notation in prose. No native/layout certificate.
rows.independent_semantic_review: Entered width/height >0 are followed by desired-image width and height each >=1px. Target-image topic plus explicit pixel units distinguishes resolved output from entered percentages. This functional restriction does not assert every positive input is valid, that input already uses pixels, or that consumer memory/source checks pass.

rows.raw: Android ti ha sedi na u ma\'usa i ramienta para un atyik dokumentu: %1$s
rows.display: Android ti ha sedi na u ma'usa i ramienta para un atyik dokumentu: %1$s
rows.linguistic_review: Negated sedi plus a finite irrealis passive means Android did not permit the chooser tool to be used. The two-argument, non-control use of sedi is explicitly supported by Chung. The purpose clause identifies a tool for selecting documents/files rather than a human picker. This preserves a launch block without inventing a permission type, permanent ban, deleted file or failed decoder. The one detail slot is unchanged.
rows.caller_review: Primary calls in ClassicPaintActivity:1101 and AssemblyActivity:195 catch SecurityException. LegacyImageCreditsActivity:120 handles the ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT launch and supplies either error.message or a localized fallback. The nested ACTION_GET_CONTENT fallback is inside the ActivityNotFoundException handler and does not reach its sibling SecurityException catch; v2 metadata correctly limits that claim.

rows.english: The picker returned no file. Please choose the file again.
rows.raw: Tåya\' dokumentu ni marisibi ginin i ramienta para un atyik dokumentu. Put fabot, atyik ta\'lu i dokumentu.
rows.display: Tåya' dokumentu ni marisibi ginin i ramienta para un atyik dokumentu. Put fabot, atyik ta'lu i dokumentu.
rows.linguistic_review: The negative existential is restricted by the received-relative and source phrase, so it says no file was received from the selecting tool, not that no file exists or was deleted. Productive ma-passive is suitable with an unspecified receiving agent. The final polite imperative preserves selection of the file again without promising success or demanding a different file. Singular/default document form is suitable here; it does not assert an exact cardinality of one.
rows.caller_review: ClassicPaintActivity.kt:1251 follows the RESULT_OK gate and tests data?.data ?: data?.clipData?.getItemAt(0)?.uri for null. This precedes the open/import/save/export switch, so the wording must remain generic to a selected file rather than image decoding.

rows.display: Tåya' dokumentu siha ni manmarisibi ginin i ramienta para un atyik dokumentu siha.
rows.linguistic_review: Plural siha plus the realis plural passive man-ma-risibi is grammatically supported. It preserves no files received from the multi-file selecting tool. It adds no retry instruction and no unsupported-file, cancellation or deletion diagnosis. The existential scopes over the received files rather than making a claim about disk contents.
rows.caller_review: AssemblyActivity.kt:201 tests an empty URI list for ADD_IMAGES and RESULT_OK before importImages. The launcher requests multiple selection; this is not a stream or decode failure.

primary_lexical_sources_actually_read.assessment: Select/choose supports the functional chooser paraphrase; no claim of an attested GUI term.
Document noun. File sense is a disclosed application extension consistent with this catalogue, not a dictionary software attestation.
General tool and receive senses; nearby ramenta hand-tool variant does not invalidate the explicit general tool entry.
Allow/permit fits a blocked chooser launch.

Repetition and negative existence support picker clauses. Decode appears among translåda glosses, but both examples concern language interpretation; that does not resolve the technical-sense ambiguity of this exact candidate.
Picture sense and polite formula supported; running examples use unaccented Put fabot.
Information/message and selected passive supported. No payload-specific sense established by these entries.
Give/provide supports the source-tool purpose phrase, not the image-data constituent by itself.

findings: Realis plural man- and passive intransitivity support manmarisibi; ma-passive singular/dual uses no -um-.
Purpose para plus irrealis un/u is supported. Prepositional para means to/for, which is insufficient to force image payload.
Passive ma- takes a glottal stop before a vowel-initial root in careful speech.
Postnominal ni relative and noun-plural siha are supported.
Affirmative transitive imperative has no agreement prefix.
Sedi has a two-argument non-control use; na plus irrealis complement is supported.
